paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, as he was praying in a certain place, that when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, even as John also taught his disciples.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tō einai auton en topō tini proseuchomenon, hōs epausato, eipen tis tōn mathētōn autou pros auton· Kyrie, didaxon hēmas proseuchesthai, kathōs kai Iōannēs edidaxen tous mathētas autou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Father, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autois· Hotan proseuchēsthe, legete· Pater, hagiasthētō to onoma sou· elthetō hē basileia sou·

paragraphs.text: Give us day by day our daily bread.
paragraphs.original: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν·
paragraphs.translit: ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion didou hēmin to kathʼ hēmeran·

paragraphs.text: And forgive us our sins; for we ourselves also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And bring us not into temptation.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai aphes hēmin tas hamartias hēmōn, kai gar autoi aphiomen panti opheilonti hēmin· kai mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen pros autous· Tis ex hymōn hexei philon kai poreusetai pros auton mesonyktiou kai eipē autō· Phile, chrēson moi treis artous,

paragraphs.text: for a friend of mine is come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him;
paragraphs.original: ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: epeidē philos mou paregeneto ex hodou pros me kai ouk echō ho parathēsō autō·

paragraphs.text: and he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee?
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.
paragraphs.translit: kakeinos esōthen apokritheis eipē· Mē moi kopous pareche· ēdē hē thyra kekleistai, kai ta paidia mou metʼ emou eis tēn koitēn eisin· ou dynamai anastas dounai soi.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will arise and give him as many as he needeth.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin, ei kai ou dōsei autō anastas dia to einai philon autou, dia ge tēn anaideian autou egertheis dōsei autō hosōn chrēzei.

paragraphs.text: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
paragraphs.original: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·
paragraphs.translit: Kagō hymin legō, aiteite, kai dothēsetai hymin· zēteite, kai heurēsete· krouete, kai anoigēsetai hymin·

paragraphs.text: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: pas gar ho aitōn lambanei, kai ho zētōn heuriskei, kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And of which of you that is a father shall his son ask a loaf, and he give him a stone? or a fish, and he for a fish give him a serpent?
paragraphs.original: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;
paragraphs.translit: tina de ex hymōn ton patera aitēsei ho hyios ichthyn, kai anti ichthyos ophin autō epidōsei;

paragraphs.text: Or [if] he shall ask an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
paragraphs.original: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;
paragraphs.translit: ē kai aitēsei ōon, epidōsei autō skorpion;

paragraphs.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall [your] heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ei oun hymeis ponēroi hyparchontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois hymōn, posō mallon ho patēr ho ex ouranou dōsei pneuma hagion tois aitousin auton.

paragraphs.text: And he was casting out a demon [that was] dumb. And it came to pass, when the demon was gone out, the dumb man spake; and the multitudes marvelled.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēn ekballōn daimonion kōphon· egeneto de tou daimoniou exelthontos elalēsen ho kōphos. kai ethaumasan hoi ochloi·

paragraphs.text: But some of them said, By Beelzebub the prince of the demons casteth he out demons.
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·
paragraphs.translit: tines de ex autōn eipon· En Beelzeboul tō archonti tōn daimoniōn ekballei ta daimonia·

paragraphs.text: And others, trying [him], sought of him a sign from heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: heteroi de peirazontes sēmeion ex ouranou ezētoun parʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house [divided] against a house falleth.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.
paragraphs.translit: autos de eidōs autōn ta dianoēmata eipen autois· Pasa basileia ephʼ heautēn diameristheisa erēmoutai, kai oikos epi oikon piptei.

paragraphs.text: And if Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.
paragraphs.translit: ei de kai ho Satanas ephʼ heauton diemeristhē, pōs stathēsetai hē basileia autou; hoti legete en Beelzeboul ekballein me ta daimonia.

paragraphs.text: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.
paragraphs.translit: ei de egō en Beelzeboul ekballō ta daimonia, hoi hyioi hymōn en tini ekballousin; dia touto autoi hymōn kritai esontai.

paragraphs.text: But if I by the finger of God cast out demons, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de en daktylō theou ekballō ta daimonia, ara ephthasen ephʼ hymas hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: When the strong [man] fully armed guardeth his own court, his goods are in peace:
paragraphs.original: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hotan ho ischyros kathōplismenos phylassē tēn heautou aulēn, en eirēnē estin ta hyparchonta autou·

paragraphs.text: but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him his whole armor wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.
paragraphs.original: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφʼ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: epan de ischyroteros autou epelthōn nikēsē auton, tēn panoplian autou airei ephʼ hē epepoithei, kai ta skyla autou diadidōsin.

paragraphs.text: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετʼ ἐμοῦ κατʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετʼ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
paragraphs.translit: ho mē ōn metʼ emou katʼ emou estin, kai ho mē synagōn metʼ emou skorpizei.

paragraphs.text: The unclean spirit when he is gone out of the man, passeth through waterless places, seeking rest, and finding none, he saith, I will turn back unto my house whence I came out.
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται διʼ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ μὴ εὑρίσκον λέγει· Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον·
paragraphs.translit: Hotan to akatharton pneuma exelthē apo tou anthrōpou, dierchetai diʼ anydrōn topōn zētoun anapausin, kai mē heuriskon legei· Hypostrepsō eis ton oikon mou hothen exēlthon·

paragraphs.text: And when he is come, he findeth it swept and garnished.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthon heuriskei sesarōmenon kai kekosmēmenon.

paragraphs.text: Then goeth he, and taketh [to him] seven other spirits more evil than himself; and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man becometh worse than the first.
paragraphs.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ, καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
paragraphs.translit: tote poreuetai kai paralambanei hetera pneumata ponērotera heautou hepta, kai eiselthonta katoikei ekei, kai ginetai ta eschata tou anthrōpou ekeinou cheirona tōn prōtōn.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the breasts which thou didst suck.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tō legein auton tauta eparasa tis phōnēn gynē ek tou ochlou eipen autō· Makaria hē koilia hē bastasasa se kai mastoi hous ethēlasas·

paragraphs.text: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.
paragraphs.translit: autos de eipen· Menoun makarioi hoi akouontes ton logon tou theou kai phylassontes.

paragraphs.text: And when the multitudes were gathering together unto him, he began to say, This generation is an evil generation: it seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it but the sign of Jonah.
paragraphs.original: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ.
paragraphs.translit: Tōn de ochlōn epathroizomenōn ērxato legein· Hē genea hautē genea ponēra estin· sēmeion zētei, kai sēmeion ou dothēsetai autē ei mē to sēmeion Iōna.

paragraphs.text: For even as Jonah became a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο Ἰωνᾶς τοῖς Νινευίταις σημεῖον, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gar egeneto Iōnas tois Nineuitais sēmeion, houtōs estai kai ho hyios tou anthrōpou tē genea tautē.

paragraphs.text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and shall condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
paragraphs.original: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: basilissa notou egerthēsetai en tē krisei meta tōn andrōn tēs geneas tautēs kai katakrinei autous· hoti ēlthen ek tōn peratōn tēs gēs akousai tēn sophian Solomōnos, kai idou pleion Solomōnos hōde.

paragraphs.text: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.
paragraphs.original: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: andres Nineuitai anastēsontai en tē krisei meta tēs geneas tautēs kai katakrinousin autēn· hoti metenoēsan eis to kērygma Iōna, kai idou pleion Iōna hōde.

paragraphs.text: No man, when he hath lighted a lamp, putteth it in a cellar, neither under the bushel, but on the stand, that they which enter in may see the light.
paragraphs.original: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φέγγος βλέπωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Oudeis lychnon hapsas eis kryptēn tithēsin oude hypo ton modion allʼ epi tēn lychnian, hina hoi eisporeuomenoi to phengos blepōsin.

paragraphs.text: The lamp of thy body is thine eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.
paragraphs.original: ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου. ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν· ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ, καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos sou. hotan ho ophthalmos sou haplous ē, kai holon to sōma sou phōteinon estin· epan de ponēros ē, kai to sōma sou skoteinon.

paragraphs.text: Look therefore whether the light that is in thee be not darkness.
paragraphs.original: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: skopei oun mē to phōs to en soi skotos estin.

paragraphs.text: If therefore thy whole body be full of light, having no part dark, it shall be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining doth give thee light.
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν, μὴ ἔχον μέρος τι σκοτεινόν, ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε.
paragraphs.translit: ei oun to sōma sou holon phōteinon, mē echon meros ti skoteinon, estai phōteinon holon hōs hotan ho lychnos tē astrapē phōtizē se.

paragraphs.text: Now as he spake, a Pharisee asketh him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρʼ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.
paragraphs.translit: En de tō lalēsai erōta auton Pharisaios hopōs aristēsē parʼ autō· eiselthōn de anepesen.

paragraphs.text: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled that he had not first bathed himself before dinner.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pharisaios idōn ethaumasen hoti ou prōton ebaptisthē pro tou aristou.

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said unto him, Now ye the Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter; but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho kyrios pros auton· Nyn hymeis hoi Pharisaioi to exōthen tou potēriou kai tou pinakos katharizete, to de esōthen hymōn gemei harpagēs kai ponērias.

paragraphs.text: Ye foolish ones, did not he that made the outside make the inside also?
paragraphs.original: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;
paragraphs.translit: aphrones, ouch ho poiēsas to exōthen kai to esōthen epoiēsen;

paragraphs.text: But give for alms those things which are within; and behold, all things are clean unto you.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: plēn ta enonta dote eleēmosynēn, kai idou panta kathara hymin estin.

paragraphs.text: But woe unto you Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God: but these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.
paragraphs.translit: Alla ouai hymin tois Pharisaiois, hoti apodekatoute to hēdyosmon kai to pēganon kai pan lachanon, kai parerchesthe tēn krisin kai tēn agapēn tou theou· tauta de edei poiēsai kakeina mē pareinai.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you Pharisees! for ye love the chief seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the marketplaces.
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.
paragraphs.translit: ouai hymin tois Pharisaiois, hoti agapate tēn prōtokathedrian en tais synagōgais kai tous aspasmous en tais agorais.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you! for ye are as the tombs which appear not, and the men that walk over [them] know it not.
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.
paragraphs.translit: ouai hymin, hoti este hōs ta mnēmeia ta adēla, kai hoi anthrōpoi hoi peripatountes epanō ouk oidasin.

paragraphs.text: And one of the lawyers answering saith unto him, Teacher, in saying this thou reproachest us also.
paragraphs.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.
paragraphs.translit: Apokritheis de tis tōn nomikōn legei autō· Didaskale, tauta legōn kai hēmas hybrizeis.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Woe unto you lawyers also! for ye load men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Kai hymin tois nomikois ouai, hoti phortizete tous anthrōpous phortia dysbastakta, kai autoi heni tōn daktylōn hymōn ou prospsauete tois phortiois.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you! for ye build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: ouai hymin, hoti oikodomeite ta mnēmeia tōn prophētōn hoi de pateres hymōn apekteinan autous.

paragraphs.text: So ye are witnesses and consent unto the works of your fathers: for they killed them, and ye build [their tombs].
paragraphs.original: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.
paragraphs.translit: ara martyres este kai syneudokeite tois ergois tōn paterōn hymōn, hoti autoi men apekteinan autous hymeis de oikodomeite.

paragraphs.text: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send unto them prophets and apostles; and [some] of them they shall kill and persecute;
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ εἶπεν· Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ διώξουσιν,
paragraphs.translit: dia touto kai hē sophia tou theou eipen· Apostelō eis autous prophētas kai apostolous, kai ex autōn apoktenousin kai diōxousin,

paragraphs.text: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
paragraphs.original: ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης,
paragraphs.translit: hina ekzētēthē to haima pantōn tōn prophētōn to ekkechymenon apo katabolēs kosmou apo tēs geneas tautēs,

paragraphs.text: from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary: yea, I say unto you, it shall be required of this generation.
paragraphs.original: ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
paragraphs.translit: apo haimatos Habel heōs haimatos Zachariou tou apolomenou metaxy tou thysiastēriou kai tou oikou· nai, legō hymin, ekzētēthēsetai apo tēs geneas tautēs.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto you lawyers! for ye took away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.
paragraphs.translit: ouai hymin tois nomikois, hoti ērate tēn kleida tēs gnōseōs· autoi ouk eisēlthate kai tous eiserchomenous ekōlysate.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come out from thence, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press upon [him] vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things;
paragraphs.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων,
paragraphs.translit: Kakeithen exelthontos autou ērxanto hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi deinōs enechein kai apostomatizein auton peri pleionōn,

paragraphs.text: laying wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.
paragraphs.original: ἐνεδρεύοντες αὐτὸν θηρεῦσαί τι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: enedreuontes auton thēreusai ti ek tou stomatos autou.
